system_description.narrative_title: Escalating drone attacks on energy and maritime infrastructure
system_description.narrative_summary: A wave of drone strikes is targeting energy and port infrastructure across multiple theaters (Egypt, Russia, Kerch Strait), widening a conflict-space from kinetic fronts into global energy and shipping routes. As an open system, hostile unmanned aerial systems (inputs) exploit infrastructure vulnerabilities (states/processes) to disrupt flows (oil, grain), generate market and insurance shocks (outputs), and provoke layered security and military responses (feedback). The dynamic links tactical strikes to strategic energy-security and supply-chain consequences.
system_description.scope: Energy and maritime infrastructure and flows at risk from drone attacks: refineries, storage tankers/terminals, grain export points, ports and chokepoints (Suez, Kerch), commercial shipping, on-site security and counter-UAS measures, insurers, commodity traders, and regional military/security actors directly responding.
system_description.super_system: Global energy and commodity security embedded in geopolitics and international trade
adjacent_subsystems: Regional military conflicts (Russia–Ukraine, Middle East/Iran–Israel dynamics)
Maritime shipping, ports and chokepoint operations (Suez Canal, Kerch Strait)
Drone proliferation and counter-UAS technology & defense logistics

variables.name: Drone attack rate
variables.description: The frequency and aggregate intensity of hostile unmanned aerial system strikes against energy and maritime infrastructure per unit time.

variables.name: Munition severity
variables.description: The average destructive potential of munitions and payloads carried by attacking unmanned systems.

variables.name: Infrastructure vulnerability
variables.description: The aggregate susceptibility of energy and maritime assets to damage or disruption from kinetic and non-kinetic attacks.

variables.name: On-site security effectiveness
variables.description: The operational effectiveness of on-site physical security, access control, and immediate incident response at infrastructure sites.

variables.name: Counter‑UAS deployment rate
variables.description: The rate at which counter-unmanned aerial systems and active mitigation measures are deployed and activated across at-risk sites and routes.

variables.name: Maritime transit flow
variables.description: The volume and rate of commercial shipping transiting key sea routes and chokepoints relevant to energy and commodity transport.

variables.name: Energy export flow
variables.description: The rate at which energy commodities (e.g., oil, refined products, gas) are shipped or exported from production/processing hubs.

variables.name: Storage utilization
variables.description: The proportion of available storage capacity for fuels and bulk commodities that is currently in use at terminals and tank farms.

variables.name: Refinery processing capacity
variables.description: The active processing capacity of refining and conversion facilities available for producing refined energy products.

variables.name: Shipping delay level
variables.description: The aggregate delays and transit-time increases experienced by commercial shipping due to threat mitigation, inspections, and rerouting.

variables.name: Insurance premia level
variables.description: The prevailing level of insurance premiums and war-risk surcharges applied to vessels, cargoes, and energy assets in the affected domains.

variables.name: Commodity price volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of price fluctuations in energy and bulk commodity markets driven by supply, demand, and risk perceptions.

variables.name: Trader hedging rate
variables.description: The rate at which market participants increase or alter hedging and risk-management positions in response to disruption signals.

variables.name: Military response intensity
variables.description: The intensity and tempo of military and armed security operations directed at deterring, interdicting, or retaliating against attacks on infrastructure and routes.

variables.name: Escalation risk perception
variables.description: The perceived probability among actors that tactical attacks will broaden into wider geopolitical or kinetic escalation affecting trade and energy security.

variables.name: ISR coverage
variables.description: The geographic and temporal coverage level of intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance assets monitoring infrastructure, routes, and actor activity.

catalysts.title: Geographic spread to Suez & Egyptian ports
catalysts.description: Attacks expand to major chokepoints and Egyptian Mediterranean ports, prompting transit risk and rerouting.
catalysts.rationale: Egypt/Suez port strikes reported (2026-07-30, 2026-07-31) imply spread to chokepoints and transit disruption.

catalysts.title: Refinery and storage outages
catalysts.description: Damage from strikes forces temporary halts at refineries and storage facilities, reducing processing and export capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Lukoil, Ryazan refinery hits and storage-tanker strike reported (2026-07-30/31), causing halts and outages.

catalysts.title: Rapid counter‑UAS and port hardening
catalysts.description: Operators and states accelerate deployment of counter-UAS, access controls and hardening at refineries and ports.
catalysts.rationale: Security concerns after Suez and port strikes (2026-07-30/31) will drive rapid C‑UAS and hardening deployments.

catalysts.title: Naval and military patrol surges
catalysts.description: Increased naval/air patrols and escorts in Suez and adjacent seas raise military tempo and route controls.
catalysts.rationale: Reports of strikes near Suez and rising threat (2026-07-31) likely trigger patrol surges and escorts.

catalysts.title: Insurance premia and war‑risk surcharge hikes
catalysts.description: Insurers raise war-risk premiums and surcharges for vessels and terminals operating in affected waters and ports.
catalysts.rationale: Widening attacks and Suez export concerns (2026-07-30/31) typically prompt insurers to raise war‑risk charges.

catalysts.title: Market hedging and price volatility spike
catalysts.description: Traders increase hedging and markets display elevated volatility in response to repeated attacks and outage reports.
catalysts.rationale: Refinery halts and Suez threat reports (2026-07-30/31) will provoke rapid hedging and price swings.
